English authored content; Hindi and Santali translations pending review.
No practical competence or recognised qualification awarded.

review.reviewMethod: Primary-source cross-check and authored scenario consistency review by an AI coding assistant; not an independent clinical assessment.

steps.title: Pause at the scene
steps.cue: An adult has collapsed in a community hall. A chair has fallen nearby.
steps.question: Before approaching, what do you check?

choices.text: Check for hazards and whether you can approach safely
Rush forward without looking
Ask everyone to leave before calling for help

steps.explanation: Notice hazards before approaching. If the area is unsafe, keep clear and summon emergency help. This simulated scene contains no electrical or traffic hazard.

steps.title: Check responsiveness
steps.cue: The area is safe. The adult does not respond to your voice or a gentle shoulder tap.
steps.question: What information matters next?

choices.text: Assume they are sleeping
Give them water
Check whether they are breathing normally and get help

steps.explanation: Responsiveness and normal breathing guide a lay responder. Do not give food or drink to an unresponsive person. This activity does not train diagnosis.

steps.title: Recognise the cue
steps.cue: The simulated adult makes occasional irregular gasps. There is no normal breathing.
steps.question: How should you interpret this?

choices.text: Wait to see if they wake up
Gasping is not normal breathing; treat this as an emergency
Gasping means normal breathing

steps.explanation: For an unresponsive adult, absent or abnormal breathing, including gasping, is a cardiac-arrest warning. A lay responder should not delay action while trying to diagnose the cause.
steps.anatomyPurpose: Explore location only; not a measurement or diagnosis of a real person.

steps.title: Give your buddy a clear task
steps.cue: A bystander is beside you. An AED is signposted nearby.
steps.question: Choose the clearest instruction.

choices.text: You in the blue shirt: call emergency services, bring the AED and report back
Somebody should do something
Go home and find medicine

steps.explanation: Address one person and specify help, equipment and a return report. In India use the local emergency response number; 112 is the integrated emergency service. No call is made by this simulation.

steps.title: Begin simulated CPR learning
steps.cue: Emergency help has been activated. The adult remains unresponsive and is not breathing normally.
steps.question: Which learning action is appropriate?

choices.text: Wait for the AED before starting CPR
Practise compressions on a classmate
Start the CPR sequence and follow dispatcher guidance

steps.explanation: CPR should begin promptly. This app teaches sequence only. Effective compressions and breaths require practical training with an appropriate manikin and instructor. Never practise compressions on another learner.
steps.anatomyPurpose: Explore location only; not a measurement or diagnosis of a real person.

steps.title: Understand the chest landmark
steps.cue: Open the body view to locate the sternum and see its relationship to the ribs.
steps.question: What can this model teach?

choices.text: Whether a real casualty has a pulse
The location of a landmark; a manikin is needed to assess compression skill
How hard I press a real chest

steps.explanation: An anatomical model supports location knowledge. Touchscreen pressure does not measure chest compression force or depth. Inspecting a structure is exploration, not a practical competency assessment.
steps.anatomyPurpose: Explore location only; not a measurement or diagnosis of a real person.

steps.title: The AED arrives
steps.cue: A virtual AED is now available. Its prompts have not yet started.
steps.question: What is the next principle?

choices.text: Turn it on and follow its instructions and pad diagrams
Guess the pad positions from memory alone
Use a phone as an AED

steps.explanation: Follow the specific AED prompts and pad illustrations. A phone cannot deliver a therapeutic shock. Pad handling and special situations require an approved practical lesson.

steps.title: Analysis and shock prompts
steps.cue: The virtual AED announces that it is analysing the rhythm.
steps.question: How do you keep the simulated action safe?

choices.text: Keep a hand on the casualty during analysis
Ignore the instructions if the screen is slow
Ensure nobody touches the casualty; follow the AED prompts

steps.explanation: Keep everyone clear during analysis and any advised shock. The scenario uses authored prompts and does not analyse a real heart rhythm.

steps.title: Continue after the prompt
steps.cue: The AED instructs the responder to resume CPR.
steps.question: Choose the next action.

choices.text: Remove the AED and walk away
Resume CPR as instructed and follow dispatcher / AED guidance
Stop permanently because the device was used

steps.explanation: Follow the AED and emergency dispatcher. A completed screen sequence is evidence of decision practice only, not proof of effective resuscitation.

steps.title: Explain what happened
steps.cue: The emergency team arrives in this scenario.
steps.question: What should your handover contain?

choices.text: What you saw, when help was called and the actions / AED prompts followed
A diagnosis you invented
Only your score in the app

steps.explanation: Report observations and actions clearly. Do not turn uncertain observations into a diagnosis. Review missed decisions and arrange hands-on training.

scenarios.title: Get help for an unwell adult

steps.title: Notice and keep safe
steps.cue: A teacher is on the floor. A spilled drink is nearby.
steps.question: What is your first action?

choices.text: Run through the spill
Try to lift the teacher alone
Keep clear of the spill and alert another responsible adult

steps.explanation: Your role in this activity is to recognise a problem, stay safe and get help.

steps.title: Communicate clearly
steps.cue: You find another teacher nearby.
steps.question: What do you say?

choices.text: I think I know exactly what disease they have
An adult has collapsed in the hall; please come and call emergency help
There is something somewhere

steps.explanation: Give the location and what you observed. A responsible adult can coordinate help. Do not guess a diagnosis.

steps.title: Make room for help
steps.cue: Adults are responding and need space.
steps.question: What can you do?

choices.text: Keep others back and follow the responsible adult’s instructions
Crowd around and film the person
Give the person food or drink

steps.explanation: Protect the person’s privacy and leave room for responders. Do not record or share images of an unwell person.

steps.title: Know your role
steps.cue: Another student asks to practise CPR on you.
steps.question: What do you say?

choices.text: Yes, if they press gently
Only if someone records it
No; compressions are practised on a training manikin with an instructor

steps.explanation: Never practise chest compressions on another learner. This awareness path does not assign adult responder responsibilities.

steps.title: Recognise uncertainty
steps.cue: You see smoke near a corridor. You do not know its source.
steps.question: What is the safe first decision?

choices.text: Assume it is harmless because the flame is small
Raise the alarm and begin the evacuation procedure
Move towards the smoke to identify the fuel

steps.explanation: Treat smoke as a warning. Report what you see and follow the local evacuation procedure. Do not approach to investigate.

steps.title: Choose a different route
steps.cue: The usual exit is obscured by smoke. An alternative signed route is visibly clear.
steps.question: Which route do you choose?

choices.text: Use the clear alternative route according to the site plan
Run through smoke because the familiar route is shorter
Take the lift to save time

steps.explanation: A familiar exit may become unusable. Use an available safe escape route and follow the site plan. Never enter smoke to complete an app task.

steps.title: Know your role
steps.cue: You have not been trained or authorised to use an extinguisher.
steps.question: Should you attempt to fight the fire?

choices.text: Yes; any extinguisher works on any fire
Yes; a phone lesson replaces practical authorisation
No; leave, alert others and seek help

steps.explanation: Extinguisher response is conditional on training, the correct equipment, a small contained fire and a safe escape route. Evacuation is the right decision when these conditions are not met.

steps.title: Keep moving to safety
steps.cue: Your bag is in a room behind you.
steps.question: What do you do?

choices.text: Ask a friend to go back for you
Leave belongings and continue to the assembly point
Return for the bag

steps.explanation: Do not let belongings delay escape or cause re-entry. Tell the responsible staff about anyone unaccounted for.

steps.title: Account for the group
steps.cue: At the assembly point a classmate is missing.
steps.question: What is your next action?

choices.text: Tell the responsible staff; do not re-enter
Go back alone to search
Assume they went home

steps.explanation: Report the missing person and their last known location. Trained responders coordinate searches; do not re-enter.

steps.title: Apply it in another place
steps.cue: At home, smoke now blocks your usual door.
steps.question: Which principle stays the same?

choices.text: Only school fires require evacuation
Find the source before alerting anyone
Use a safe available escape route and get help; do not enter smoke

steps.explanation: The exact exit changes with the building. Recognition, alerting, safe escape and staying out remain the priorities. Learn the plan for each place.

steps.title: Check response conditions
steps.cue: Adult workplace simulation: the alarm is raised, emergency help is being called, smoke is not affecting you and your escape route is clear.
steps.question: What else must be true before considering extinguisher use?

choices.text: You are trained and authorised; the fire is small and contained; the correct unit is available
An extinguisher is nearby, which is enough
You have finished this app, which authorises you

steps.explanation: Only a trained, authorised and physically able responder should consider an attempt. Smoke, uncertainty, unsuitable equipment or a threatened exit mean evacuation. This lesson does not authorise firefighting.

steps.title: Read the unit label
steps.cue: A virtual extinguisher has a label describing its approved uses. The fuel is uncertain.
steps.question: Which decision is appropriate?

choices.text: Choose water for every fire
Treat all class letters as identical in every country
Do not guess agent suitability; withdraw and report uncertainty

steps.explanation: Classification systems vary. Read the approved local label and site training. This scenario does not apply US class letters to Indian equipment.

steps.title: Find the hidden fault
steps.cue: The virtual inspection card shows a missing safety seal and a damaged hose.
steps.question: What should you do with this unit?

choices.text: Repair it during the emergency
Do not use it; report the fault and maintain a safe exit
Ignore the fault and operate it

steps.explanation: Condition checks matter. Damaged or uncertain equipment should not be treated as serviceable. Choose withdrawal when an appropriate serviceable unit is unavailable.

steps.title: Check the right indicators
steps.cue: The selected virtual unit is a stored-pressure extinguisher with a gauge. Its pointer is outside the marked operating range.
steps.question: What does this change?

choices.text: Treat this unit as unavailable and report it
Use it because the cylinder looks full
Assume every extinguisher has the same gauge

steps.explanation: Inspect the indicators and instructions for that model. Not all extinguisher types have a pressure gauge.

steps.title: Understand operation
steps.cue: For an appropriate, serviceable unit, the trained responder follows its operating label.
steps.question: What does the common PASS mnemonic describe?

choices.text: Press the gauge and shake the cylinder
Spray towards smoke regardless of the fire base
Pull, aim, squeeze, sweep — subject to the unit’s instructions

steps.explanation: PASS is an operating reminder, not permission to approach a fire. Use the specific unit’s label and practical training. The equipment lab lets you inspect the components.

steps.title: Conditions change
steps.cue: Smoke increases and your escape route is becoming threatened.
steps.question: What action takes priority?

choices.text: Move deeper into the room
Stop the attempt and evacuate immediately
Continue until the extinguisher is empty

steps.explanation: A changing scene invalidates the earlier decision to respond. Stop and retreat while escape is still possible.

steps.title: Handover observations
steps.cue: You are safely at the assembly point.
steps.question: What do you report?

choices.text: Location, observed conditions, equipment fault and people at risk
A guaranteed cause of the fire
That the building is safe because flames are no longer visible

steps.explanation: Report observable facts. Only the responsible emergency personnel can authorise re-entry. This app does not determine real-scene safety.

scenarios.title: A serious bleeding injury
objectives: Recognise the limits of screen practice

steps.title: Approach with care
steps.cue: An alert adult has a bleeding forearm after broken glass. You have checked the scene.
steps.question: What do you say first?

choices.text: Start filming the wound
Promise you can diagnose the injury
Introduce yourself and ask to help

steps.explanation: Explain your actions and respect the person. Use gloves or another suitable barrier when available.

steps.title: Control the bleeding
steps.cue: Heavy bleeding continues. No object is visible in this wound.
steps.question: Choose the immediate response.

choices.text: Remove pressure repeatedly to inspect it
Apply firm direct pressure with a dressing or clean cloth; get emergency help
Wash the wound for several minutes before applying pressure

steps.explanation: Heavy bleeding needs prompt pressure and emergency help. A helper can call while pressure continues.

steps.title: A different wound
steps.cue: In the next example, a glass fragment remains embedded.
steps.question: What changes?

choices.text: Leave it in place and press beside it, not onto it
Pull it out to see the wound
Push it deeper to stop the blood

steps.explanation: An embedded object may be limiting blood loss. Removing it can worsen bleeding.

steps.title: Pressure is not enough
steps.cue: The simulated limb bleed continues despite firm pressure.
steps.question: What should happen next?

choices.text: Release pressure and leave the casualty
Assume the phone score means bleeding is controlled
Tell the dispatcher and follow further bleeding-control guidance

steps.explanation: Escalation may need trained tourniquet use. This lesson does not teach application or certify pressure technique.

steps.title: Keep the handover factual
steps.cue: A responder takes over.
steps.question: What information is useful?

choices.text: An invented diagnosis
Where bleeding started, pressure applied and changes observed
A guessed blood-loss volume

steps.explanation: Screen choices record decisions only. Hands-on bleeding-control practice needs suitable training equipment and supervision.

scenarios.title: A hot-water burn
objectives: Recognise when to get urgent help

steps.title: Stop further injury
steps.cue: An adult has spilled hot water on their forearm. The kettle is no longer a hazard.
steps.question: What starts care?

choices.text: Cover it tightly before cooling
Move away from the heat and cool the affected area
Apply cooking oil

steps.explanation: This case is a thermal scald. Chemical and electrical burns need a different response.

steps.title: Choose cooling
steps.cue: Cool running water is available.
steps.question: How should this thermal burn be cooled?

choices.text: Use cool running water for 20 minutes
Press ice directly onto the skin
Cool only until the pain first eases

steps.explanation: Start cooling promptly. Keep the rest of the person warm; do not chill their whole body.

steps.title: Check clothing and jewellery
steps.cue: A loose bracelet is nearby, but fabric is stuck to the burn.
steps.question: What should you do?

choices.text: Pull off the stuck fabric
Rub cream into the burn
Remove loose nearby items; leave stuck fabric in place

steps.explanation: Avoid further skin damage. Do not use butter, oils or creams, or burst blisters.

steps.title: After cooling
steps.cue: The burn has cooled. A clean covering is available.
steps.question: Choose the suitable principle.

choices.text: Rub the injured skin dry
Cover loosely with an appropriate non-stick covering
Wrap the limb tightly with adhesive material

steps.explanation: Do not use an adhesive dressing directly on the burn. A cover should not constrict the limb.

steps.title: Recognise a different severity
steps.cue: A second example has a large, deep burn on the face.
steps.question: What is needed?

choices.text: Urgent medical help
The same home-care-only plan
A camera diagnosis

steps.explanation: Large, deep, facial, chemical or electrical burns need urgent assessment. When unsure, seek medical advice.

scenarios.title: Unresponsive but breathing
objectives: Understand the purpose of a side-lying position

steps.title: Choose the correct branch
steps.cue: The adult is unresponsive but breathing normally. There is no suspected injury. Help is being called.
steps.question: Which care principle fits?

choices.text: Maintain the airway using a recovery position and monitor
Start compressions despite normal breathing
Give water to wake them

steps.explanation: A recovery position supports an open airway in this situation. It is not the cardiac-arrest branch.
steps.anatomyPurpose: Explore location only; not a measurement or diagnosis of a real person.

steps.title: Inspect the airway
steps.cue: Use the body view to find the trachea.
steps.question: What does this exploration prove?

choices.text: A real person can breathe because the mesh is visible
I can skip hands-on positioning practice
I can identify a structure, not assess a real airway

steps.explanation: The body view is an anatomical reference. Positioning another person requires practical technique and care.
steps.anatomyPurpose: Explore location only; not a measurement or diagnosis of a real person.

steps.title: Keep checking
steps.cue: After positioning, the adult now makes occasional gasps instead of normal breaths.
steps.question: What changes?

choices.text: Give food to restore energy
Treat gasping as abnormal; follow emergency guidance and start CPR
Leave them alone in the same position

steps.explanation: The earlier decision no longer applies. Reassess breathing and act on the change; do not mistake gasps for normal breathing.
steps.anatomyPurpose: Explore location only; not a measurement or diagnosis of a real person.

steps.title: Do not generalise the manoeuvre
steps.cue: A different casualty has fallen from height and may have a spinal injury.
steps.question: Should you routinely roll them as in the earlier case?

choices.text: No; minimise movement and get emergency guidance, prioritising the airway
Yes; every unconscious person is rolled the same way
Keep the airway blocked to avoid any movement

steps.explanation: Suspected trauma changes the approach. Airway needs can require movement; follow dispatcher guidance and trained assistance.

scenarios.title: An adult is choking
prerequisites: Adult casualty only; pregnancy and inability to encircle the abdomen need an adapted technique
Use training equipment and an instructor for hands-on practice
objectives: Recognise collapse and seek follow-up care

steps.title: Notice the change
steps.cue: An adult coughs strongly after food enters their airway and can still speak.
steps.question: What is appropriate?

choices.text: Immediately start abdominal thrusts
Give water to push the food down
Encourage coughing and watch closely

steps.explanation: An effective cough may clear the obstruction. Be ready to help if the cough becomes ineffective.
steps.anatomyPurpose: Explore location only; not a measurement or diagnosis of a real person.

steps.title: The cough becomes silent
steps.cue: The adult cannot speak, breathe or cough effectively. A helper can call for help.
steps.question: Which simulated sequence fits severe adult choking?

choices.text: Wait silently for them to recover
Get emergency help; give up to five back blows, then up to five abdominal thrusts if needed
Ask them to swallow more food

steps.explanation: Stop if the blockage clears; otherwise repeat the sequence while responsive. Practise physical technique only with an instructor and training equipment.

steps.title: Avoid a harmful shortcut
steps.cue: You cannot see any object in the mouth.
steps.question: Should you sweep your fingers inside blindly?

choices.text: No
Yes, every time
Only if somebody films it

steps.explanation: Blind sweeps can worsen obstruction. Do not search with fingers for an unseen object.

steps.title: The adult becomes unresponsive
steps.cue: The severe choking has not cleared. The adult collapses.
steps.question: What should happen?

choices.text: Keep the person standing for more thrusts
Wait for them to cough again
Start CPR with compressions and ensure emergency help has been called

steps.explanation: The response changes with loss of responsiveness. Follow dispatcher guidance; do not apply this adult lesson to infants.
steps.anatomyPurpose: Explore location only; not a measurement or diagnosis of a real person.

steps.title: The blockage clears
steps.cue: Abdominal thrusts were used and the person is breathing again.
steps.question: What is the next care principle?

choices.text: Immediately resume eating
Arrange medical evaluation and continue to observe
Assume no injury is possible

steps.explanation: Thrusts can cause injury. This adult example excludes pregnancy and cases where the abdomen cannot be encircled; those need an adapted technique.

scenarios.title: Protect during a seizure
objectives: Keep objects out of the mouth

steps.title: Reduce injury risk
steps.cue: An adult falls and has jerking movements beside a chair.
steps.question: What is helpful?

choices.text: Drag them across the room without danger present
Move nearby hazards and cushion the head if safe
Hold the person down

steps.explanation: Give space, note the start time and protect privacy. Do not restrain them.
steps.anatomyPurpose: Explore location only; not a measurement or diagnosis of a real person.

steps.title: Reject the mouth myth
steps.cue: A bystander offers a spoon to put in the person’s mouth.
steps.question: What do you do?

choices.text: Stop them; put nothing in the mouth
Accept the spoon
Give a drink instead

steps.explanation: Objects, fingers and drinks can cause harm. Do not force the mouth open.

steps.title: Recognise an emergency
steps.cue: This is the person’s first known seizure.
steps.question: When should help be requested?

choices.text: Only after they return to work
Never for a seizure
Now; call emergency services

steps.explanation: Emergency help is also needed for prolonged or repeated seizures, injury or abnormal breathing. Follow an existing care plan when appropriate.

steps.title: The movements stop
steps.cue: The person is no longer jerking.
steps.question: What should you check?

choices.text: Whether they can eat immediately
Responsiveness and whether breathing is normal
Only whether they remember their name

steps.explanation: Monitor and reassure. Unresponsive but normally breathing calls for airway care; absent or abnormal breathing calls for CPR and emergency guidance.

steps.title: Give a useful handover
steps.cue: Help arrives.
steps.question: What can you report reliably?

choices.text: Start time, duration, movements and breathing changes
That they definitely have epilepsy
A video shared publicly

steps.explanation: Observation supports responders. One episode does not establish its cause.

scenarios.title: A painful arm after a fall

steps.title: Do not test the injury
steps.cue: An adult has a painful, swollen forearm after a fall. The scene is safe.
steps.question: What should you avoid?

choices.text: Asking them to move it to prove whether it is broken
Reassuring them
Arranging assessment

steps.explanation: Support the injured area in a comfortable position. A normal-looking limb does not rule out a fracture.

steps.title: Keep the limb supported
steps.cue: The arm looks deformed.
steps.question: Which response is appropriate?

choices.text: Pull it straight
Massage firmly over the injury
Keep it supported and seek medical care

steps.explanation: Do not try to realign a suspected fracture. Practical support and sling skills require supervised learning.

steps.title: Spot a warning sign
steps.cue: There is an open wound over the injury and the hand feels numb.
steps.question: How does this affect urgency?

choices.text: Push any visible bone back in
Get emergency medical help
Wait until tomorrow

steps.explanation: Open injuries or altered sensation require urgent assessment. Never push protruding bone back into place.

scenarios.title: Match the hazard, not the colour

steps.title: A burning pan
steps.cue: There is a pan fire in a home kitchen. You are not trained to tackle it.
steps.question: Which response is appropriate?

choices.text: Throw water into the pan
Carry the pan outside
Get out, stay out and call for help; do not move the pan

steps.explanation: Water can violently spread burning oil. Do not move a burning pan or approach it to complete this lesson.

steps.title: An energised appliance
steps.cue: A damaged appliance is burning. You cannot safely reach its isolator.
steps.question: What should you do?

choices.text: Touch the appliance to check whether it is live
Keep clear, raise the alarm and evacuate
Pour a bucket of water over it

steps.explanation: Electrical involvement adds a shock hazard. Do not approach to isolate power when that would expose you to danger.

steps.title: Compare two labelled units
steps.cue: Adult workplace exercise: a trained responder identifies a small paper fire with no electrical involvement. A clear exit and safe conditions are confirmed.
steps.question: What establishes agent suitability?

choices.text: The unit’s approved label for this fuel and the site procedure
The brightest cylinder colour
The closest cylinder, regardless of its label

steps.explanation: Different agents serve different hazards. Read the local label; an appearance or country’s class lettering alone is not enough.

steps.title: Reject a universal rule
steps.cue: A learner says a sand bucket is suitable for every fire.
steps.question: Which answer is sound?

choices.text: Yes; sand always replaces an extinguisher
Yes, provided the bucket is coloured red
No; suitability depends on the hazard and approved site training

steps.explanation: Do not generalise one site’s equipment to every fuel. Unknown suitability means no attempt and safe withdrawal.

steps.title: The scene is uncertain
steps.cue: You cannot identify the fuel or confirm a safe exit.
steps.question: Which choice demonstrates good judgement?

choices.text: Move closer to get a better phone picture
Evacuate and report the uncertainty
Try each agent until one works

steps.explanation: A valid decision can be to decline an attempt. Scoring should not reward firefighting when conditions are unsuitable.

steps.title: The alarm sounds
steps.cue: During class, the fire alarm starts. The teacher directs your group to leave.
steps.question: What should you do?

choices.text: Go looking for an extinguisher
Follow the evacuation instructions and leave belongings
Finish the lesson first

steps.explanation: This awareness path is about alerting, leaving and getting help. Children are not assigned firefighting tasks.

steps.title: The usual exit is blocked
steps.cue: Your group’s usual route has smoke. A responsible adult directs you to a clear alternative.
steps.question: What is appropriate?

choices.text: Use the safe alternative with the group
Push through the smoke
Separate from the group to collect a bag

steps.explanation: Know more than one route. A route must be usable now, not simply familiar.

steps.title: Reach the meeting point
steps.cue: A classmate is not accounted for.
steps.question: What should you do?

choices.text: Return to search alone
Ask another student to re-enter
Tell the teacher the last place you saw them; stay out

steps.explanation: Accountability gives responders useful information. Never re-enter to search or collect belongings.

plannedChapters: Supervised CPR and AED skill assessment
